p.seg: Yǐn Gōng
In the first year, in spring, the king's first month.
What is meant by "first year"?
It is the beginning year of the ruler.
What is meant by "spring"?
It is the beginning of the year.
Whom do we call "king"?
We are referring to Wén Wáng.
Why do we mention "king" before "first month"?
It is the king's first month.
What is meant by saying "the king's first month"?
It signifies great unification.
Why doesn't the Duke mention his enthronement?
It is to fulfill the Duke's intention.
What intention of the Duke does it fulfill?
The Duke intended to pacify the state and return it to Huán.
Why return it to Huán?
Huán was young but noble,
Yǐn was older but of lower status.
Their difference in status was subtle,
and the people of the state did not understand.
Yǐn was older and also virtuous.
The various senior officials supported Yǐn and established him.
Yǐn, therefore, declined to be established,
because he was not sure that Huán would necessarily be able to be established.
Moreover, if Huán were established,
then there was fear that the various high officials would not be able to assist the young ruler,
therefore, the general establishment of Yǐn was in fact the establishment of Huán.
Yǐn was older and more virtuous,
why was he not suitable to be established?
In establishing an heir, one establishes the eldest, not the virtuous;
in establishing a son, one establishes the noble, not the eldest.
How was Huán noble?
His mother was noble.
If the mother was noble, how was the son noble?
The son is noble because of the mother,
the mother is noble because of the son.
In the third month,
the Duke and Yí Fù of Zhū Lóu made a covenant at Mèi.
What does "jí (及)" mean?
It means "yǔ (與)," to participate.
"Huì (會)," "jí (及)," and "jì (暨)" all mean "yǔ (與)."
Why are they sometimes called "huì (會),"
sometimes "jí (及),"
and sometimes "jì (暨)"?
"Huì (會)" is like "zùi (冣)," a gathering;
"jí (及)" is like "jíjí (汲汲)," eagerly pursuing;
"jì (暨)" is like "jìjì (暨暨)," grudgingly.
"Jí (及)" indicates I desire it;
"jì (暨)" indicates it's unavoidable.
Who was Yí Fù (儀父)?
He was the ruler of Zhū Lóu.
Why is he named by his style name?
It is his style name.
Why is he referred to by his style name?
To commend him.
Why commend him?
Because he made a covenant with the duke.
There were many who made covenants with the duke,
why commend only this one?
Because he was worthy of commendation, he was commended.
How was he worthy of commendation?
He advanced gradually.
What is "Mèi"?
It is a place name.
In the fifth month of summer,
The Earl of Zhèng conquered Duàn in Yān.
What does "conquered" mean?
It means to kill him.
If he killed him, why is it called "conquered"?
To magnify the wickedness of the Earl of Zhèng.
Why magnify the wickedness of the Earl of Zhèng?
His mother wanted to establish him,
and he himself killed him,
it would have been better not to give him anything.
Who was Duàn?
He was the younger brother of the Earl of Zhèng.
Why is he not referred to as "younger brother"?
Because he was in charge of the state.
Where was his territory?
He was in charge of the state.
Why is the killing of Wúzhī by the people of Qí not recorded with his territory?
Because it happened within the state.
If it happened within the state, even if he was in charge of the state, it is not recorded with his territory.
If he was not in charge of the state, even if he was outside, it is also not recorded with his territory.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the Son of Heaven sent the Zǎi Xuǎn to deliver the gifts of condolence for Huì Gōng and Zhòngzǐ.
What is *zǎi*?
It is an official title.
What is *xuǎn*?
It is a name.
Why is the official title used as a surname?
Because he was a *zǎishì* (steward).
Who is Huì Gōng?
He is the father of Yǐn.
Who is Zhòngzǐ?
She is the mother of Huán.
Why is she not referred to as *fūrén* (madam)?
Because Huán had not yet become ruler.
What are *fèng*?
*Fèng* are part of funeral rites.
*Fèng* generally include horses and chariots, along with bundled silks.
Chariots and horses are called *fèng*,
Goods and wealth are called fù (賻).
Clothing and bedding are called suì (襚).
If Huán (桓) was not yet the ruler, why would the various lords come to present fèng (賵)?
Yǐn (隱) established Huán.
Therefore, he announced the mourning of Huán's mother to the various lords.
Then what does "爾" (ěr) mean?
It's the intention of Chéng Gōng (成公).
Why does it say "來" (lái, come)?
It didn't involve matters of state.
Why does it say "Huì Gōng's (惠公) second son"?
It combines them.
Combining them is not in accordance with ritual.
Why is there no mention of "jí zhòng zǐ" (及仲子, and the second son)?
The second son was of humble status.
In the ninth month,
they made an alliance with the people of Sòng (宋) at Sù (宿).
Who is included in "jí zhī" (及之, and them)?
Those of low status among those included.
In the twelfth month of winter,
Jì Bó (祭伯) came.
Who is Jì Bó?
He is a grand officer of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he not referred to as a "shǐ" (使, envoy)?
He fled.
If he fled, then why does it not say "bēn" (奔, fled)?
The king has no outside,
saying "fled" implies there is a term for "outside."
Gōngzǐ Yì Shī died.
Why is the day not recorded?
Because it was far away.
Different wording for what was seen,
different wording for what was heard,
different wording for what was passed on by hearsay.
In the spring of the second year,
the Duke met with the Róng people at Qián.
In the fifth month of summer,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
What does "entered" mean?
It means they obtained it but did not hold it.
Wú Hài led his troops into Jí.
Who is Wú Hài?
He is Zhǎn Wú Hài.
Why is his clan name not used?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
It is to show disdain for the beginning of the destruction.
Did the beginning of the destruction originate here?
Before this.
Before this, then why begin here?
To entrust the beginning there.
Why entrust the beginning there?
It is the beginning of the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals).
This is an omission.
What is the reason for including this?
It's to conceal a great internal evil.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day *gēngchén*,
the Duke and the Róng people made a covenant at Táng.
In the ninth month,
Jǐ Lǚxū came to meet the bride.
Who is Jǐ Lǚxū?
He is a *dàfū* (official) of Jǐ.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
In marriage ceremonies, the host is not referred to.
Then what is the appropriate title?
One refers to paternal relatives, elder brothers, teachers, and friends.
When the Duke of Sòng sent Gōngsūn Shòu to present betrothal gifts,
why was he referred to as the host?
Because the reasoning is exhausted.
What does "reasoning is exhausted" mean?
It means there was no mother.
Then does Jǐ have a mother?
Yes.
If there was a rule, why not mention the mother?
The mother is not relevant here.
When a daughter is met with adversity abroad, it is not recorded.
Why is it recorded here?
To censure.
What is being censured?
Censure for initially not personally welcoming (the bride).
Did the initial failure to personally welcome (the bride) originate here?
It was before this.
If it was before this, then why is it considered the beginning here?
It is taken as the starting point.
Why is it taken as the starting point?
Because it is the beginning of the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals).
Why is a woman sometimes called "nǚ" (女, daughter)?
Sometimes called "fù" (婦, wife)?
Sometimes called "fūrén" (夫人, madam)?
In her own state, she is called "nǚ" (女, daughter).
On the road, she is called "fù" (婦, wife).
Upon entering the state, she is called "fūrén" (夫人, madam).
In the tenth month of winter,
Bó Jī (伯姬) was sent in marriage to Jǐ (紀).
Who is Bó Jī (伯姬)?
She is an inner woman (a daughter of the ruling house).
Why is it said "guī" (歸, returned)?
For women, marriage is called "guī" (歸, returning).
Jì Zǐbó and the ruler of Jǔ made a covenant at Mì.
Who was Jì Zǐbó?
He is not known.
In the twelfth month, on the day yǐmǎo,
Lady Zǐshì died.
Who was Lady Zǐshì?
She was the mother of Duke Yǐngōng.
Why is her burial not recorded?
To fulfill the intention of the Duke.
How was the Duke's intention fulfilled?
Because Zǐ (Duke Yǐngōng) would not ultimately become the ruler,
therefore his mother would also not ultimately be the Lady.
The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi.
In the spring of the third year, the royal second month, on the day jǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
Why is it recorded?
To record an anomaly.
Why is it that sometimes a day is specified in relation to the solar eclipse, and sometimes not?
Why is it that sometimes the first day of the month (shuò) is specified, and sometimes not?
When it says, "On the first day (shuò) of a certain month on a certain day,
there was a solar eclipse,"
it means the eclipse occurred on the true first day of the month.
The reason why sometimes a day is specified and sometimes not
Some lose it before, and some lose it after.
Losing it before means the *shuò* (朔, new moon) is ahead;
losing it after means the *shuò* is behind.
In the third month, *gēngxū*,
the Heavenly King died.
Why is the burial not recorded?
With the Son of Heaven, the record focuses on death and not burial,
it must be at the proper time.
With the feudal lords, the record notes both death and burial,
because there is a Son of Heaven still in existence,
and they are not allowed to decide on the proper time themselves.
Why do some say *bēng* (崩, collapse) and some say *hōng* (薨, demise)?
The Son of Heaven is referred to as *bēng*,
the feudal lords are referred to as *hōng*,
the grand masters are referred to as *zú* (卒, death),
and the scholars are referred to as *bùlù* (不祿, without emolument).
In the summer, the fourth month, *xīnmǎo*,
the *Yǐn* clan died.
Who was the *Yǐn* clan?
He was a grand master of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as the *Yǐn* clan?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
To criticize hereditary ministers;
Hereditary ministers, that is not in accordance with ritual.
When a *wài dàfū* (outer grandee) does not die in office,
how can this be considered dying in office?
The death of the Son of Heaven is the responsibility of the lords.
Autumn,
the son of the Wǔ lineage came to request a funeral grant.
Who is this "son of the Wǔ lineage"?
He is a grandee of the Son of Heaven.
Why refer to him as "son of the Wǔ lineage"?
Censure.
What censure is it?
The father has died, but the son has not yet received his official appointment.
Why not refer to him as "envoy"?
Because he is in mourning and not yet a ruler.
Why is it recorded that the son of the Wǔ lineage came to request a funeral grant?
Censure.
What censure is it?
Funerals are not a time for requests;
requesting a funeral grant is not in accordance with ritual;
it insinuates that he is trying to influence those below.
In the eighth month, on the day *gēngchén*,
Duke Hé of Sòng died.
In the twelfth month of winter,
Qí Hóu (齊侯), Zhèng Bó (鄭伯) formed an alliance at Shímén (石門).
On guǐ wèi (癸未),
the burial of Sòng Mù Gōng (宋繆公) took place.
Why are some burials announced with a specific date, and others not?
Announcing a date when it's not yet the proper time indicates [anxiety for a] rushed burial.
It is a hasty burial.
Not announcing a date when it's not yet the proper time indicates a negligent burial.
It is a slow burial.
Announcing a date after the proper time indicates covering something up.
It is concealing it.
Not announcing a date after the proper time indicates being unable to perform the burial properly.
It's called being unable to bury.
Not announcing a date at the proper time is correct.
Announcing a date at the proper time indicates a precarious situation preventing a proper burial.
What was the danger at this time?
Xuān Gōng (宣公) said to Mù Gōng (繆公):
"Considering my love for my daughter,
it is not as great as my love for Yǔ Yí (與夷).
But if we are to consider who should be the master of the state altars and ancestral temple,
then Yǔ Yí (與夷) is not as good as my daughter.
Why not finally be the ruler?"
Xuān Gōng (宣公) died.
Mù Gōng (繆公) ascended the throne.
Mù Gōng (繆公) banished his two sons, Zhuāng Gōng Féng (莊公馮) and the Grand Tutor Bó (勃), saying:
"Since you are my sons,
let us not see each other in life,
nor mourn each other in death."
"Do not weep for each other in death."
Yǔ Yí 夷復 said,
"The reason why the late lord did not give the state to me but submitted the state to you,
was because he believed that you could be the master of the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple.
Now, you have driven away your two sons and are about to entrust the state to me, Yǔ Yí.
This is not what the late lord intended.
Moreover, if sons can be expelled,
then the late lord would have expelled me long ago."
Duke Mù 繆公 said,
"It is evident that the late lord did not expel you.
I am only ruling here as a regent."
In the end, he entrusted the state to Yǔ Yí.
Zhuāng Gōng 莊公, Féng 馮, assassinated Yǔ Yí.
Therefore, the gentleman values residing in righteousness.
The disaster of Sòng 宋 was caused by Duke Xuān 宣公.
In the fourth year, spring, second month of the king.
The people of Jǔ 莒 attacked Qǐ 杞 and
seized Móu Lóu 牟婁.
What is Móu Lóu?
It is a town of Qǐ.
The taking of towns outside the state is not recorded.
Why is this recorded?
It is recorded because this was the first time a town was taken.
On Wùshēn 戊申,
Wèi Zhōu Xū assassinated his ruler Wán.
Why is it recorded with the state name as a family name?
Because he was in control of the state.
In summer,
the Duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
What does "met" mean?
It means they did not arrange to meet.
One ruler went out,
and another ruler invited him.
The Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, men of Cài, and men of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
In autumn,
Huī led troops and joined with the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, men of Cài, and men of Wèi to attack Zhèng.
Who is Huī?
He is Gōngzǐ Huī.
Why isn't he called "Gōngzǐ"?
It is a degradation.
Why is he degraded?
Because he was involved in the assassination of the Duke.
How was he involved in the assassination of the Duke?
Gōngzǐ Huī flattered Yǐn Gōng,
and said to Yǐn Gōng:
"The people are at peace with you,
the lords are pleased with you,
why not finally become the ruler?"
Yǐn said,
"I refuse.
I will have a long coat made,
and I will grow old there."
Gōngzǐ Huī feared that his words would reach Huán,
so he said to Huán,
"I have spoken to Yǐn on your behalf.
Yǐn said,
'I will not return.'"
Huán said,
"Then what should be done?"
He said,
"Please create a difficulty
and assassinate Yǐn Gōng."
They assassinated Yǐn Gōng at the sacrifice at Zhōngwū.
In the ninth month,
the people of Wèi killed Zhōu Xū in Pú.
Why is he referred to as "person"?
It is a phrase for denouncing a traitor.
In the twelfth month of winter,
the people of Wèi established Jìn.
Who is Jìn?
He is Gōngzǐ Jìn.
What does "established" mean?
"Established" means that he should not have been established.
What does "zhēng rén hé" (其稱人何) mean?
It is a phrase referring to the one whom the multitude establishes.
Then who established him?
Shí Què (石碏) established him.
Shí Què (石碏) established him,
then what does "zhēng rén hé" (其稱人何) mean?
It refers to the one whom the multitude desires to establish.
Although the multitude desires to establish him,
their establishing him is wrong.
In the fifth year, in spring,
the Duke watched fish at Táng (棠).
Why is it written?
It is a criticism.
What is being criticized?
Remoteness.
Why would the Duke go far to watch fish?
To ascend and come.
The Duke displays a fish worth a hundred gold.
What does "dēng lái zhī zhě" (登來之者) mean?
It is a phrase praising its beauty and size.
What is Táng (棠)?
It is a town on the Jì (濟) River.
In summer, the fourth month,
the funeral of Duke Huán (桓公) of Wèi (衛).
In the autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Shèng.
Why is it that sometimes it is written "leading the army" and sometimes it is not?
It is either to show respect for a large army, and therefore state that someone "led the army,"
or to show respect for a small army, and therefore state "general,"
or to show contempt for a large army, and therefore state "army,"
or to show contempt for a small army, and therefore state "person."
When it is the ruler who is leading, it is not written "leading the army,"
but rather the importance of the matter is recorded.
In the ninth month,
[Kǎo] entered the palace of Zhòngzǐ.
What does "entering the palace" mean?
"[Kǎo]" means entering the inner chamber;
it was the first time sacrificing to Zhòngzǐ.
If [Huán] was not yet the ruler, why sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ?
Yǐn established Huán,
therefore, the sacrifice was made to Huán's mother.
Then why say it this way?
It was to fulfill Duke Chéng's intention.
At the first offering, six yŭ were used.
What does "first" mean?
It means beginning.
What are "six yŭ"?
They are a dance.
Why is the use of "six yŭ at the first offering" written down?
Criticism.
What is being criticized?
The criticism is that (the Ji clan) initially overstepped the bounds of the dukes.
How does the six-row dance represent overstepping the bounds?
The Son of Heaven uses eight rows of dancers,
the dukes use six,
and the feudal lords use four.
Who are these "dukes"?
Who are these "feudal lords"?
The Son of Heaven's Three Dukes are called "Duke";
descendants of former kings are called "Duke";
the remaining large states are called "Marquis";
small states are called "Earl," "Viscount," and "Baron."
Who are the Son of Heaven's Three Dukes?
They are the Son of Heaven's advisors.
If they are the Son of Heaven's advisors, why are there three?
The territory east of Shǎn is governed by the Duke of Zhōu;
the territory west of Shǎn is governed by the Duke of Shào;
one advisor resides within (the court).
Did the Ji clan's overstepping of the dukes begin with this?
It happened before this.
If it happened before this, why does it begin here?
Overstepping the dukes can still be discussed,
but overstepping the Son of Heaven cannot be discussed.
1.5.5 The people of Zhūlóu and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
1.5.6 *Míng* (a type of crop pest).
Míng,
why is it written?
It records a disaster.
In the twelfth month of winter, on the day of xīnsì,
Gōngzǐ Kōu died.
The people of Sòng attacked Zhèng,
and besieged Chánggé.
Cities are not usually described as being besieged,
so why is "besieged" mentioned here?
Because they were strong.
In the spring of the sixth year,
the people of Zhèng came to deliver a settlement.
What is "delivering a settlement"?
"Delivering a settlement" is like undoing an agreement.
Why is it said to be "undoing an agreement"?
Because they broke their agreement.
They said, "Our agreement is broken."
We and the people of Zhèng ultimately did not reach an agreement.
Why did we and the people of Zhèng ultimately not reach an agreement?
In the battle of Hú Rǎng,
Yǐngōng gained something.
So why is the battle not mentioned?
To avoid mentioning the gain.
In the fifth month, *xià wǔ yuè*, *xīn yǒu*,
the Duke (*gōng*) met with the Marquis of Qí (*Qí Hóu*) and formed an alliance at Ài.
In the seventh month, autumn.
Why is this written when nothing happened?
Although nothing happened in the *Chūnqiū*,
it is written when the beginning of the season has passed.
Why is it written when the beginning of the season has passed?
The *Chūnqiū* is arranged chronologically,
and only when the four seasons are complete does it constitute a year.
In winter,
the people of Sòng (*Sòng rén*) took Chánggé.
The taking of a city outside the state is not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
It was a long time.
In the seventh year, in the third month of spring,
Shū Jī (*Shū Jī*) returned to Jǐ (*Jǐ*).
The Marquis of Téng (*Téng Hóu*) died.
Why is his name not given?
Because it was a minor state.
If it was a minor state, why is he called "Marquis"?
There is no avoidance.
The *Chūnqiū* does not avoid using the same titles for noble and base,
nor does it avoid using the same words for good and bad.
Summer,
the city enclosed Zhōngqiū 中丘.
What is Zhōngqiū 中丘?
It is an邑 (yì) within the city.
Why is "the city enclosed Zhōngqiū 中丘" written?
To emphasize the writing.
The Marquis of Qí 齊 sent his younger brother Nián 年 to come for a state visit.
Why is he referred to as a younger brother?
A younger brother by the same mother is called "younger brother,"
an older brother by the same mother is called "older brother."
Autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu 邾婁.
Winter,
the Son of Heaven sent Fán Bó 凡伯 to come for a state visit.
The Róng 戎 attacked Fán Bó 凡伯 at Chǔqiū 楚丘
and took him back.
Who is Fán Bó 凡伯?
He is a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
This was a state visit;
why is it written that he was "attacked"?
It means he was captured.
If he was captured, why is it written that he was "attacked"?
To magnify the event.
Why is it emphasized as "great"?
It does not align with the Yí Dí (夷狄, non-Chinese tribes) controlling the Zhōngguó (中國, Central States).
What about its land?
It is emphasizing its greatness.
In the spring of the eighth year,
the Gōng (公, Duke) of Sòng (宋) and the Hóu (侯, Marquis) of Wèi (衛) met at Chuí (垂).
In the third month,
the Bó (伯, Count) of Zhèng (鄭) sent Yuǎn (宛) to return Bǐng (邴).
What is Yuǎn?
It is an insignificant person from Zhèng.
What is Bǐng?
It is a cleansing and bathing town belonging to Zhèng.
The Son of Heaven had affairs at Mount Tài (泰山),
and the various feudal lords all followed him.
At the foot of Mount Tài,
the various feudal lords all had cleansing and bathing towns there.
On the day of Gēngyín (庚寅),
we entered Bǐng.
Why does it say "entered"?
It was difficult.
What about the day?
It was difficult.
Why does it say "we"?
Saying "we" does not only mean us;
Qí (齊) also desired it.
In the sixth month, on the day jǐ hài,
Marquis Kǎo Fǔ of Cài died.
On the day xīn hài,
the Viscount of Sù died.
In the seventh month, on the day gēng wǔ,
the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Qí, and the Marquis of Wèi made a covenant at Wǎwū.
In the eighth month,
Duke Xuān of Cài was buried.
Why is the death recorded with the name, but the burial not with the name?
The death follows the correct (formality),
while the burial follows the master (deceased).
Why is the death recorded with the day, but the burial not with the day?
The death is reported urgently, but the burial is not announced.
In the ninth month, on the day xīn mǎo,
the Duke made a covenant with the people of Jǔ at Bāo Lái.
Why did the Duke make a covenant with the insignificant?
When a person is mentioned, it is because he is considered worthy and beyond doubt.
There were cutworms.
In the twelfth month of winter,
Wú Hài died.
This was Zhǎn Wú Hài.
Why is he not referred to by his clan name?
Because the practice of using clan names was just beginning to disappear,
therefore he did not use a clan name for his entire life.
In the spring of the ninth year,
the King of Heaven sent Nán Jì to pay a formal visit.
In the third month, on the day Guiyou,
there was heavy rain, thunder, and lightning.
Why is it recorded?
To record a strange occurrence.
What was strange about it?
It was out of season.
On the day Gengchen,
there was heavy snow.
Why is it recorded?
To record a strange occurrence.
What was strange about it?
It was extraordinarily heavy.
Xiá died.
Who was Xiá?
This is because my grand master had not yet received his official appointment.
Summer,
the city of Láng was built.
Autumn, seventh month.
Winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Bǐng.
Tenth year, spring, second month of the king,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and the Count of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
Summer,
Huī led the army to meet with the people of Qí and the people of Zhèng to attack Sòng.
This is Gōngzǐ Huī,
why is he not called Gōngzǐ?
Demotion.
Why demotion?
He is a criminal of Duke Yǐn.
Therefore, at the end of the chapter on Duke Yǐn, there is a demotion.
Sixth month, rénxū day,
